features.name: Noachis Terra
features.description: One of the oldest surviving geological landmasses on Mars, defining the Noachian geological epoch.
features.science: Heavily bombarded highland terrain dating back 4.1 to 3.7 billion years ago.

features.name: Arabia Terra
features.description: Extensive, densely cratered upland region in northern Mars with unique eroded plateaus.
features.science: Proposed site of supervolcano calderas that blanketed early Mars in thousands of cubic kilometers of ash.

features.name: Valles Marineris
features.origin: General name of the system of canyons honoring the scientific team of the Mariner 9 program.
features.description: The largest canyon system in the solar system: 4,000 km long, 200 km wide, and up to 7 km deep. It would stretch across the entire United States.
features.science: Formed by tectonic rifting associated with the Tharsis bulge. Contains layered sedimentary deposits suggesting ancient lakes. Water-carved side channels indicate past water flow.

features.name: Utopia Planitia
features.description: A vast, circular plain in the northern lowlands, site of the Viking 2 and Zhurong landings.
features.science: SHARAD radar discovered a subsurface water-ice reservoir as large as Lake Superior beneath Utopia.

features.name: Acidalia Planitia
features.description: Vast dark northern lowland plain known for frequent baroclinic dust storm flushing channels.
features.science: Contains extensive mud volcano candidate mounds and periglacial patterned ground.

features.name: Hellas Planitia
features.description: The deepest and one of the largest impact basins in the solar system. 7.2 km below the datum with the highest atmospheric pressure on Mars (over 1,155 Pa).
features.science: High atmospheric pressure means liquid water could potentially be stable on the surface during warm periods. Contains glacial features and possible ancient lake deposits.

features.name: Isidis Planitia
features.description: Ancient impact basin on the boundary between the southern highlands and northern lowlands.
features.science: Jezero Crater is situated on its western rim. The basin floor preserves extensive phyllosilicates.

features.name: Olympus Mons
features.description: The tallest known volcano and mountain in the solar system. 21.2 km high and 624 km across — nearly the size of France. Its caldera has six nested collapse craters.
features.science: Shield volcano formed by persistent hotspot volcanism. Some lava flows on its flanks are only a few million years old. Lava tubes may provide radiation shelter for future habitats.

features.name: Alba Mons
features.description: A low-profile volcanic construct with the largest surface area of any volcano on Mars (over 1,600 km across).
features.science: Formed by extremely low-viscosity basaltic lava flows surrounded by extensive ring grabens (Alba Fossae).

features.name: Arsia Mons
features.description: The southernmost of the Tharsis Montes volcanoes with an enormous 110-km wide caldera.
features.science: Features candidate cave entrances and lava tubes identified by THEMIS along its eastern flank.

features.name: Ascraeus Mons
features.description: The northernmost and highest of the three Tharsis Montes shield volcanoes, standing over 18 km high.
features.science: Has the lowest caldera pressure on Mars after Olympus Mons. Contains extensive parasitic cinder cones.

features.name: Elysium Mons
features.description: The principal volcano in Elysium Planitia, rising 12.6 km above the surrounding plains. Has an unusual conical shape compared to the flatter Tharsis shield volcanoes.
features.science: A stratovolcano-like shield with steep slopes. InSight landed about 1,400 km to the south-west.

features.name: Pavonis Mons
features.description: Central shield volcano of the Tharsis Montes triad, located almost precisely on Mars equator.
features.science: Rises 14 km above the datum. Exhibits low-slope shield morphology with extensive flank lava tubes.

features.name: Planum Boreum
features.description: Mars northern polar ice cap, consisting of permanent water ice layered with dust. Surrounded by the vast sand dune sea of Olympia Undae.
features.science: Layered ice deposits preserve a record of Mars climate cycles over millions of years, driven by changes in orbital obliquity (Milankovitch cycles).

features.name: Gale
features.description: A 154 km crater containing Mount Sharp (Aeolis Mons), a 5.5 km central mound of layered sediments. Curiosity has been climbing it since 2014.
features.science: Layers in Mount Sharp record billions of years of Martian climate history. Curiosity found ancient streambeds, organic molecules, and methane variations suggesting geological or biological processes.

features.name: Korolev
features.description: A northern impact crater filled with a permanent, 1.8 km thick dome of pure water ice. A natural cold trap prevents the ice from sublimating.
features.science: Contains ~2,200 km3 of water ice — about as much as Great Bear Lake in Canada. Key resource target for future Martian settlements and ISRU propellant production.

features.name: Jezero
features.description: A 45 km impact crater that once held a lake fed by river channels. Contains a well-preserved river delta — one of the best places to search for ancient biosignatures.
features.science: Clay minerals (smectite) in the delta indicate prolonged water-rock interaction. Carbonate deposits along the crater rim may preserve microbial fossils. Perseverance is actively exploring here.

features.name: Victoria
features.origin: Town in the Republic of Seychelles.
features.description: An 800-meter impact crater in Meridiani Planum explored by the Opportunity rover for 22 months. Its scalloped rim reveals exposed sulfate bedrock.
features.science: HiRISE imaged Opportunity at the crater rim. Exposed rock layers proved water was present over extensive geological epochs.
